steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Following borders are off by default (FLAGS.OPT_OFF): a new profile has only the first border. Switched on, there is one ring, 0.08 mm inside the first border.

first_offset is the gap to the first border, following_offset the gap between two following borders. The same sub-groups as for the first border are added: Layer skip, Line stipple and Start point shift.

lines: // Off by default. first_offset: distance from the first border (mm),
// following_offset: distance between two following borders (mm). An
// offset a bit smaller than the track width (0.08 mm here) lets the
// rings overlap, so there is no gap between them.
// alternate_per_contour: reverse the direction from ring to ring.

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: The group becomes part.border_following. The dialog name border_count becomes count.

steps.title: Where every ring runs
notes: compute_insets measures every ring from the original outline: ring i lies at first + first_offset + (i − 1) · following_offset. With b = 0.06 and 0.08 mm offsets: 0.14, 0.22 and 0.30 mm, exactly as in the video.
Fill contours and the hatch continue inside the innermost following border, so three borders move the hatch from 0.11 mm to 0.35 mm.

lines: // Ring i (1-based): first_offset from the first border, then one
// Fill contours continue inside the innermost border.

steps.title: One offset per ring
notes: process_contour_rings serves both following borders and fill contours. Every ring is a fresh offset of the island by its inset (make_contour_hatch), not an offset of the previous ring.
Where the part is too narrow for an inset, the offset is empty and that ring simply ends; in the 1 mm tab the hatch strip in the middle is only 0.3 mm wide.

lines: function process_contour_rings(a_ctx, a_island, a_result, a_cfg, a_insets, a_bsid, a_bsid_ds, a_split, a_isl_info)
let l_split_info = { islid: a_isl_info.islid, bounds: a_isl_info.bounds, ds: a_isl_info.ds, split: a_split };
// The ring is empty if the island is too small for this inset;
emit_contour(a_ctx, a_result, l_res.hatch, a_cfg, i, a_bsid, a_bsid_ds, l_split_info);

steps.title: Direction and seed of each ring
notes: emit_contour passes the ring index on: with alternate_per_contour neighbouring rings run in opposite directions, and every ring gets its own random start point, so the seams of the rings do not line up.
The section shows why the 0.08 mm spacing is smaller than the track: neighbouring rings overlap and leave no unmelted powder between them.

lines: function emit_contour(a_ctx, a_result, a_hatch, a_cfg, a_ring, a_bsid, a_bsid_ds, a_isl_info)
// The ring index is part of the seed, so every ring gets its own start point.
// a_bsid * 1000 + a_ring keeps the values of different contour types
let l_seed = RANDOM.make_seed(a_ctx.layer_nr, a_isl_info.islid, a_bsid * 1000 + a_ring);
// Odd layer / ring indices request a flip (index % 2 === 1).
// flip(false, true): flip every contour, keep the order of the contours.
// A missing start_point object is treated like 'off' (keep the start
// point that the geometry functions produced).
// 'random_previous' gets a random start here as a first guess; the
// post-processing may move it again based on the previous layers.
// The seed is derived from layer, island and ring, so the result is
// reproducible: recalculating a layer gives the same start points.
// For closed polygons one of the existing polygon points is chosen.

steps.title: Laser settings and order
notes: Following borders (BSID 200) run at 180 W and 800 mm/s, between the hatch and the first border in energy. Scan order 70 places them after the fill contours (60) and before the first border (80): the part is exposed from the inside out.

recipes.title: Two following borders in every new profile
recipes.why: A thicker, denser wall is the standard for your parts.
recipes.result: New profiles start with the group switched on and two rings at 0.14 and 0.22 mm. Set Following borders to 2 in Try it to see the result.

recipes.title: Spacing for a wider melt track
recipes.why: With a track of about 0.15 mm the rings can be further apart and still overlap.
recipes.result: Rings 0.1 mm apart. Check the overlap in the Section view: 0.10 mm spacing still overlaps a 0.12 mm track by 20 µm.

recipes.title: Alternate the direction from ring to ring
recipes.why: Opposite directions on neighbouring rings even out the heat input along the wall.
recipes.result: Ring 1 and ring 2 now run in opposite directions on every layer (on top of the per-layer flip).

recipes.title: Slower following borders
recipes.why: More energy per mm for a denser outer wall.
recipes.result: Following border default 700 mm/s. For one profile, change Scanning › Following border › speed in the dialog instead.
